A debit card spends money you have. A credit card spends money you borrowed.
Only the borrowed one builds your credit score.

What's the difference between a correction and a bear market?
A correction: at least 10% off the high, usually over in months. A bear market: at least 20%, and recovery often took years.
Scary words, exact numbers.

Saving keeps your number still. Investing lets it move, both ways.
At 2% inflation, 100 buys half a video game in 35 years.

A market order guarantees the trade, not the price. A limit order guarantees the price, not the trade.
In a fast market, that gap is real money.

Leverage is a ratio. Margin is real money, locked up.
At 1:100, a 10,000 position locks up 100 of your cash.

What's the difference between going long and going short?
Long: buy at 100, sell at 130, you made 30. Short: borrow and sell at 100, buy back at 70, you made 30.
But a stock can only fall to zero. It can rise forever.

Win rate counts how often. Expectancy counts how much.
70% winners can still lose money. 38% winners can still make it.

You set the stop. The exchange sets the liquidation.
At 20x leverage, a 5% move against you is enough.

Isolated risks one position. Cross risks the whole account.
Same trade, same size — very different worst case.

The spread is on your screen before you click. Slippage only shows up after.
One you can see coming. The other lands in the statement.

What's the difference between a margin call and a liquidation?
A margin call is a warning: add money, or close it yourself.
A liquidation is the exchange closing it for you. On crypto exchanges, nobody waits for your answer.
One gives you a choice. The other gives you a receipt.

What's the difference between a stop loss and a trailing stop?
A stop loss stays where you put it. A trailing stop follows the price up, and never comes back down.
Buy at 100, stop at 95, price climbs to 120: the stop loss still sits at 95. The trailing stop moved to 115.
Share this with your best mate who keeps watching a winner turn back into a loser.

What's the difference between a stop loss and a daily loss limit?
A stop loss protects one trade. A daily loss limit caps the whole day.
Daily limit 5,000. Three trades, each stopped at 2,000. Every stop worked. The day is at 6,000. Challenge over.
Most failed prop challenges die on a drawdown rule, not on the profit target.

What's the difference between leverage and liquidation?
Leverage is how big your trade is. Liquidation is how close the end is.
At 10x, roughly a 10% move against you ends the trade. At 50x, 2%. At 100x, 1%. Bitcoin moves 1% while you make coffee.
The leverage number is not your size. It is your distance to zero.
Share this with your best mate who just switched to 100x because 20x felt slow.

What's the difference between a liquidation and auto-deleveraging (ADL)?
Liquidation closes a losing trade. ADL closes a winning one.
In a crash, losers get liquidated faster than the exchange can close them. The insurance fund runs dry. So the exchange takes it from the winners: your trade, closed early, at a price you did not pick.
Share this with your best mate who thinks being right is enough on a futures exchange.

What's the difference between a maker fee and a taker fee?
A maker waits in the order book. A taker takes what is already sitting there.
Buy $10,000 of Bitcoin as a taker and you pay about $5. As a maker, about $2. Same coin, same size, same price. Only the way in was different.
Do that 200 times a year and the gap is $600.
Share this with your best mate who market-buys everything and wonders where his edge went.

What's the difference between your balance and your equity?
Balance is what you deposited. Equity is what you would have if you closed everything right now.
Fund $1,000, sit $300 down on an open trade, and your balance still says $1,000. Your equity says $700.
The exchange does not watch the balance. It watches the equity. That is the number that triggers a liquidation.
Share this with your best mate who checks the comfortable number and thinks he is fine.

What's the difference between a break-even stop and a trailing stop?
Both start in the same place: buy at 100, stop at 95. Price climbs to 120.
The break-even stop moves once, to your entry, and stays. The trailing stop keeps following, five below the high. Price falls back: one closes at 100 with nothing, the other at 115 with 15.
Same trade. The only difference is how often the stop moved.
Share this with your best mate who moves his stop to break-even and calls it risk management.

What's the difference between interest and a funding rate?
Interest is what you pay to borrow. A funding rate is what you pay to hold.
On a perpetual futures exchange, every 8 hours one side pays the other. At 0.01% on a $10,000 position that is $1, three times a day. Hold it a month and you paid $90 without a single trade.
And when the crowd is long, the longs pay.
Share this with your best mate who holds perps for weeks and wonders where the money went.

What's the difference between slippage and a gap?
Slippage happens in seconds: you buy at 100, the fill comes at 100.30.
A gap happens while the market is closed: you hold at 100 with a stop at 95, bad news overnight, the market opens at 88. Your stop fills there, not at 95.
One costs cents. The other jumps right over your stop.

What's the difference between a stop loss and a mental stop?
One is an order. The other is a decision.
Buy at 100, line at 95. The stop loss sits in the order book: at 95 the exchange closes you, watching or not. The mental stop sits in your head: at 95 you decide. Maybe it bounces. 93. Maybe now. You close at 90.
One cost 5. The other cost 10, plus a decision at the worst moment.
Share this with your best mate who says he has a mental stop and closes at 90 every time.

What's the difference between profit and realized profit?
Buy at 100, it climbs to 130. Your screen shows +30. You have not sold. It slides back to 95, and now it says -5.
Nothing was yours until you closed. One number moves with the market. The other only moves when you click.
Share this with your best mate who screenshots his open P&L.

What's the difference between risk and a stop?
Most people say: my stop is 5%, so my risk is 5%.
Account 10,000, position 1,000, stop 5% below: if it hits you lose 50. Half a percent of the account. Put all 10,000 in with the same stop and the same 5% costs 500.
The stop never changed. The size did.

What's the difference between a loss and a drawdown?
A loss is measured from where you entered. A drawdown is measured from your highest point.
Fund 1,000, grow it to 1,500, watch it fall to 1,200: you are still up 200, and you are in a 20% drawdown at the same time.
Prop firms and funds count the second number.
Share this with your best mate who is up on the year and about to fail his challenge anyway.

It feels like the market is against you. The market does not know you exist.
It feels like one more trade will fix it. One more trade is one more row.
It feels like everyone else is winning. Everyone else only posts the green days.
It feels like you are already too late. Forty trades in is early.

Feelings are data too. Log them next to the trade.

What's the difference between a stop loss and a stop hunt?
Your stop is one order. A stop hunt is thousands of them in the same place.
A stock sits at 100, most stops sit at 99.90. Price dips to 99.85, every one of them fires, the selling pushes price down for a moment, and then it snaps back to 101.
Nobody hunted you. Your stop was standing in a crowd.

That is the only audience that matters.

What's the difference between a loss and a cost?
A loss is a trade that went against you. A cost is what you pay even when it goes your way.
Win ten trades in a row, 5 each: +50. Every trade cost 6 in spread and commission: -60. Ten wins, minus 10.
You can win every trade and still lose money.
Share this with your best mate who counts wins and never counts the fees.

What's the difference between a winning streak and an edge?
A streak is what happened. An edge is what happens on average.
Flip a coin 100 times and you will get five heads in a row at some point. Nobody calls that skill. Five winning trades in a row feel like skill. Over 100 trades, the coin does that too.
Your last five trades are a story. Your last 100 are the truth.
Share this with your best mate who is on fire this week.

What's the difference between a stop loss and a hedge?
A stop closes the trade. A hedge opens a second one against it.
Long at 100, it drops to 95. A stop takes the 5 and it is over. A hedge shorts at 95, and now you are frozen: whichever way it moves, one side loses what the other makes. The 5 is still gone. You just pay fees on two positions to keep it.
Share this with your best mate who hedges instead of admitting the loss.

Which difference should I explain next? 👇

#stoploss #hedging #riskmanagement #daytrading #forex #cryptotrading #futures #tradingtips #tradingjournal #knowthedifference

The cost of a trade is five things. Only one of them is printed on your screen.

Spread: the gap you cross the moment you enter.
Slippage: the price you did not get.
Commission: the one on the receipt, usually the smallest.
Funding: the rent for holding a perpetual, every eight hours.
Overnight: the swap for holding through the night.

Which one did you never see? Comment the word.
Save this for the next time a free trade costs money, and send it to the one trader who only counts commission.

What's the difference between a call and theta?
A call is what you bought. Theta is what it loses every day you hold it.
Buy a call for 200 on Monday. The stock does not move all week. Friday, the call is worth 120. Nothing happened, and you lost 80.
Theta is the rent you pay for waiting.
Share this with your best mate who buys weeklies and waits.

What's the difference between Bitcoin and a Bitcoin ETF?
Bitcoin is the coin. The ETF is a share of a fund that holds the coin for you.
Bitcoin trades 24 hours, 7 days. The ETF trades 9:30 to 4, Monday to Friday. Bitcoin drops 8 percent on a Saturday: coin holders can sell at 2 a.m., ETF holders wait until Monday morning.
Same coin, different clock.

What hour did you last check the price? Comment the number.

What's the difference between a stop loss and a take profit?
One closes the trade when you were wrong, the other when you were right.
Buy at 100, stop at 95, target at 110. Price dips, most traders move the stop to 93. Price rises, most traders take the profit at 105. The stop gets wider, the target gets closer. That is why the plan and the account never match.

Which one do you move more often? Comment STOP or TARGET.

#stoploss #takeprofit #riskmanagement #daytrading #swingtrading #forex #cryptotrading #tradingpsychology #tradingjournal #knowthedifference

What's the difference between a drawdown and a trailing drawdown?
A drawdown is measured from your starting balance. A trailing drawdown is measured from your highest point.
Start at 100,000 with a 5,000 limit and make 4,000. Static: you can still lose 9,000. Trailing: the floor moved up with you, you can lose 5,000. Same account, same profit, different floor.

Which one does your firm use? Comment STATIC or TRAILING.

#propfirm #drawdown #trailingdrawdown #fundedtrader #riskmanagement #daytrading #futures #forex #tradingjournal #knowthedifference

What's the difference between a loss and a losing streak?
A loss is one trade. A streak is what one loss does to the next trade.
You lose 50, that was the plan. You lose 50 again, now you want it back. Trade three is bigger, faster, and outside the plan. The first two losses cost 100. The third one costs the week.

After three losses in a row, what do you do? Comment TRADE or CLOSE.

#tradingpsychology #losingstreak #riskmanagement #daytrading #swingtrading #forex #cryptotrading #tilt #tradingjournal #knowthedifference

What's the difference between a revenge trade and a re-entry?
Both happen right after a loss. A re-entry has a reason on the chart. A revenge trade has a reason in your chest.
Stopped at 95. Price comes back and breaks the level again: re-entry, same size, same stop. Price does nothing, but you need the 5 back: revenge, double size, no stop. Same click, different trader.

Which one was your last trade after a loss? Comment CHART or CHEST.

#revengetrading #tradingpsychology #riskmanagement #daytrading #swingtrading #forex #cryptotrading #tilt #tradingjournal #knowthedifference

You remember the big win. The journal remembers the ten before it.
You remember a terrible month. The journal remembers it was one week.
You remember “I always get stopped out.” The journal says it was three times.

Memory keeps the story. The journal keeps the numbers.

You are not a reliable witness. Everyone's memory works this way, it keeps what felt loud and drops what was ordinary. That is why traders write it down.

Save this for the next time you are sure about a pattern you never counted, and send it to the one trader who trades from memory.

#tradingpsychology #tradingjournal #daytrading #swingtrading #riskmanagement #forex #cryptotrading #tradingmindset #knowthedifference

What's the difference between a stop loss and the spread?
Your stop is a price. The spread is the gap between the two prices you actually get.
Stop at 95. The chart shows 95.20 and never lower. You still get stopped out. The chart shows the last trade, your stop fires on the bid, and during news the spread widened from 1 to 4. The chart never touched 95. The bid did.

How wide is your spread during news? Comment the number.

#stoploss #spread #forex #daytrading #scalping #cryptotrading #riskmanagement #tradingtips #tradingjournal #knowthedifference

Follow for more differences.

What's the difference between a loss and a gap?
A loss is what you planned to risk. A gap is what the market does while it is closed.
Buy at 100, stop at 95, bad news overnight. The market opens at 88 and your stop fires at the first price. You planned to lose 5. You lost 12. A stop is a promise the market only keeps while it is open.

What was your worst gap? Comment the number.

#stoploss #gap #swingtrading #daytrading #stockmarket #forex #riskmanagement #tradingtips #tradingjournal #knowthedifference

Follow for more differences.

What's the difference between a stop loss and a wick?
Your stop is a line. A wick is how far price went before it came back.
Stop at 95, right under the last low. The candle dips to 94.80 for three seconds, then closes at 99. You are out, and the candle looks fine. The wick is where the orders were, yours included. Put the stop where the wick would have to be wrong.

How far below the low is your stop? Comment the number.

#stoploss #wick #priceaction #daytrading #forex #cryptotrading #riskmanagement #tradingtips #tradingjournal #knowthedifference

A tighter stop feels safer. What it actually changes is your size.

100 shares with the stop 5 below: risk 500. Stop 1 below, so you buy 500 shares: risk 500. Same money on the line, five times the chance of being stopped out before the move.

Most traders will disagree with this one. Tell me where I'm wrong.

#stoploss #positionsizing #riskmanagement #daytrading #tradingjournal

The free trade that cost you the trade.

Buy at 100, stop at 95. Price reaches 103, the stop goes to 100, and it feels like nothing can go wrong now. Then 99, stopped out, then 110 without you. A stop loss protects the account. A break-even stop protects your feelings, and it charges you the trades that needed room.

Most traders swear by it. Tell me where I'm wrong.

#breakeven #stoploss #swingtrading #tradingpsychology #tradingjournal

Lose 10 percent and you need 11 to get back. Lose 50 percent and you need 100. The recovery is always bigger than the loss, and that is why one bad stretch takes so long to undo.

What is your worst drawdown? Comment the number.

#drawdown #riskmanagement #tradingpsychology #daytrading #tradingjournal

A stop loss asks where. A time stop asks how long.

Buy at 100 with a stop at 95. Three weeks later it is still 100. Nothing hit your stop, and nothing happened, while your money sat in a trade that had no reason to exist. A time stop closes it on day five.

How long do you hold a trade that does nothing? Comment the days.

#timestop #stoploss #swingtrading #riskmanagement #tradingjournal

A cash account spends your money. A margin account spends the broker's money too.

Say you have 10,000 and the stock falls 40 percent. In the cash account you are down 4,000, and nothing else happens. On margin you bought 20,000 worth, so the same drop leaves 12,000, and 10,000 of that is the loan. Your 10,000 became 2,000, and the broker can close the position without asking you first.

Same stock, same 40 percent. The difference is who decides when you are out.

Cash or margin? Comment which one you trade.

Short selling is one trader borrowing a share and selling it. A short squeeze is all of them buying it back at once.

Sell at 100 and buy it back at 70, you made 30. Sell at 100 and watch it run to 200, you lost 100. And you cannot wait it out, because the borrowed share has to be returned. So you buy. That buying lifts the price, which forces the next short to buy.

A long can lose everything. A short has no ceiling to lose against.

Ever been squeezed? Comment the ticker.

A track record shows what happened. Survivorship bias is everything that never made it into the screenshot.

Take 1,000 traders who only flip a coin. After ten days, about one of them is green every single day. That one posts the screenshot. The other 999 delete the app.

Every strategy you copy was picked because it survived. Your own history is the only record where nothing was deleted.

How many losing months are in yours? Comment the number.

Apple's new folding iPhone costs 1,999 dollars. Four hundred market orders cost the same.

Taking the price that is already there costs about 0.05 percent on the big exchanges. Waiting for it costs about 0.02. On a 10,000 dollar trade that is five dollars against two. Four hundred times a year, and you paid for the phone.

Same trade, same price, same day. Only the button was different.

Send this to the one who market-buys everything.

Market or limit? Comment which one you use. 👇

The most expensive habit in trading takes one second: moving the stop.

A stop at −2 % dragged down to −12 % is six times the planned loss. If your average winner is +2 %, that single trade erased six of them.

The stop is a decision you already made. Moving it is a new one, taken by the worst version of you.

Send this to the friend who says „it will come back".

Have you ever moved a stop? 👇

#stoploss #riskmanagement #tradingpsychology #tradingjournal #knowthedifference

Your prop account says $100,000. Your real buffer is $5,000.

The challenge gives you a $10,000 trailing drawdown, so it feels like $10,000 of room. But you touched $105,000 once, and a trailing drawdown follows the peak upward. Your floor moved to $95,000. Half the drawdown is spent before you place a trade.

The floor climbs with every equity high. It does not climb back down for you.

Send this to the friend who is on his third challenge and still blames the strategy.

What is your real buffer right now? 👇

#propfirm #trailingdrawdown #riskmanagement #tradingjournal #knowthedifference

Lose half your account and you need +100 % just to get back to flat.

Down 10 % you need 11 %. Down 25 % you need 33 %. Down 50 % you need 100 %. Every step down steepens the climb, because the money left to do the climbing got smaller.

The size of the position is the part you set before the trade. The depth of the hole is the part you never get to choose.

Send this to the friend who says he will make it back next week.

What is your hard stop for a bad week? 👇

#drawdown #riskmanagement #positionsizing #tradingjournal #knowthedifference
